title: Atlas admits it scores 3 of 12 declared sources

Root cause is precise: they land in kg_node/kg_edge, whose provenance is a free-text jsonb blob rather than the source plus ingest_run_id quartet, so they are neither scored by the atlas nor Merkle-sealed by the ledger. Commit 4c37087 declares all twelve with the landing each one's rows reach and derives the nine unscorable, at zero new store reads. An unscored source deliberately carries NO number: four 'unrated' scores would assert 'this source has no rows in the store', which is false. Scoring kg_* was ruled out of scope - it would break the integrity rule's own printed claim.

title: Atlas printed rule is now byte-bound to the constant that scores

Live risk, not theory: the last four commits in that area were i18n catalog rounds, so a copy-polish pass would silently have made the human page print a different rule than the machine endpoint publishes. Commit b3aa8cb keeps the catalog as the RENDER source and the constant as the PUBLISH source, and asserts the Czech string AFTER ICU substitution is byte-identical to ATLAS_RULES while the English must NOT equal it and must pass looksEnglish - one pin holding both the drift risk and the do-not-leave-English-reading-Czech risk. First messages.test.ts for the feature.

body: No skip affordance existed anywhere in the app. AppShell renders the rail before content in the DOM, so a keyboard or screen-reader user walked 13 minimum and about 23 maximum tab stops before main on every one of ~23 non-bare routes. The landmark skeleton was already correct (aside, named nav, main in all 38 page components) - the only missing thing was an element to jump between them with. Commit 774dcf6: one component, one catalog key, targeting an #obsah wrapper in the CHROME rather than 38 identical ids on each page's own main, with tabIndex -1 because without it Firefox and Safari scroll but leave focus in the rail. features/shell/a11y.test.ts: 7 assertions, 7 source mutations, 7 caught.

title: Catalog boundary lint now covers all of features/shared

Commit 760fed2 widens the glob, verified by probe in both directions: two synthetic cross-imports pass under the old scope and fail under the new one, and repo-wide lint is unchanged at 0 errors / 12 warnings. The durable lesson: tightening a boundary that is already broken means either exemptions or a big cleanup; tightening it while it still holds costs nothing, so the no-op moment IS the right moment.

title: Review console stopped losing the reviewer's note on its own advertised keyboard path
body: /penize/kontrola gates 211 pending decisions and every decision is appended to a tamper-evident hash chain. The advertised 1/2/3 shortcuts called handleDecide with a null note while the mouse path sent the draft, which lived inside ReviewCard and was unreachable from the parent's window listener - and the note is the ONLY thing that survives a decision into the chain, while needs-more without a note is a documented no-op that writes nothing at all. So a reviewer could type a reason, blur the field, press 2, and believe a tie had been flagged when nothing happened. Commit 919cbcb lifts the draft to a ref in the parent, makes handleDecide the one place a note is resolved, and refuses to submit a note-less needs-more. graphTraversal was deliberately NOT imported, with the reason written into a doc comment: that rule is planar, this queue is 1-D.

title: Sentinel: added an 'unevaluable' status, made an erased audit chain a violation, and stopped the workflow rendering green with zero invariants evaluated
body: The instrument built because a wrong ranking shipped for six days could not distinguish 'checked and clean' from 'never looked'. SentinelCheckStatus was ok|violation only, so report.ts rendered every non-violation as PASS. verifyReviewChain filters `where chain_pos is not null`, so nulling the column emptied the set and the invariant returned 'chain is empty - trivially valid': ERASING the whole tamper-evident ledger scored greener than altering one row. And the dispatched workflow gated its run step on a guard, but a skipped step does not fail a job, so ubuntu-latest produced a green check with 0 of 11 invariants evaluated. Now: sentinelVerdict() is the ONE derivation read by evaluator, unreadable path and parser; countReviewAudit compares chained rows to the whole ledger; run.ts writes a schema-valid all-unevaluable report on the unreadable path (exit 2). Verified live: exit 2, verdict 'unevaluable', artifact written where the old code wrote nothing. STILL UNCOVERED: the money and law layers have zero invariants. Commit 821a107.

title: All 211 money ties claimed their class was 'written by an analysis pass or a human review, not guessed' - both halves false for the whole live corpus
body: Proved from the write path, not by argument: ReviewRepository.setTieReviewState (the only write path of /penize/kontrola) builds nextProps from review_state/last_decision/last_reviewer/last_reviewed_at/review_note - tie_class is not among them, so NO stored class can be a human decision. Payload census: batch-002 wrote 245 tie_class values via classifyTie, batch-006 two more, only 15 (batch-001) from real registry research. The graph carries no tie_class_provenance, so which pass wrote a given class is unknowable and the copy now says so. Consequence of the drift between the four copies of the heuristic: Vodovody a kanalizace Vsetin/Vyskov carry `manager` because the writing pass's marker table lacked 'vodovody a kanalizace', and isAttributable (tieClass !== steward) therefore hangs two municipal water utilities' public contract volume on named MPs. classifyTie + its marker tables now have ONE definition, imported by the three scripts. No stored value rewritten. Commits 8cc7e65, c14e32b.

New server-component 404 distinguishes the two explicitly and routes by WHAT was sought; it deliberately prints no status numeral because Next returns 404 only for non-streamed responses. Both boundaries dropped 'Hlaseni jsme odeslali'/'A report has been sent' (Sentry is DSN-gated to a no-op; this repo has no DSN). global-error's real lang defect was that only 2 of 7 English fragments carried lang=en. robots.txt now publishes the sitemap. And sidebarParts.tsx imported the mock catalog for ONE .name lookup, shipping invented persons and invented ICOs in a 14 615 B chunk the layout loads everywhere; module names moved to navModel.ts. Measured over a controlled two-build A/B from served HTML: six routes -14 652 B each, 8 of 23 routes now clean (15 keep it via their own importers). Fraunces was preloaded everywhere at 126 928 B (47% of the font payload) with one grep hit, its own declaration: preloaded 270 316 -> 143 388 B. Commits cc16ee8, 52f0f4a.

title: The impossible-date boundary was forked four ways, letting /rozpocty publish a municipality's contract history running to 2043
body: plausible-date.ts says in its header it exists so the bound is 'v cele aplikaci jedna a stejna'. It was not. /rozpocty carried a private y>1900 && y<2100 fork, and the CHECKED-IN municipalSuppliers.generated.ts holds 00279676 x Ceskoslovenska obchodni banka spanning 2009-2043. yearOf ran at GENERATION time, so the gate had to go at the DECODE boundary to affect the live page; the upper bound is now SUPPLIERS_RETRIEVED_ON (the day the register was read) rather than 'today', and both bounds are withheld together because withholding one would be an estimate. /penize/[pspId] printed signedOn verbatim while its sibling company page suppressed and disclosed the same field, and /penize/[pspId]/paket baked impossible dates into a hash-stamped downloadable bundle. datedFacts.ts re-declared PLAUSIBLE_FROM and deriveDenik.ts imported it THROUGH datedFacts; both now read the canonical module. Design note worth keeping: the raw signedOn STAYS on MoneyMpDetail because profileMoney.ts recomputes its own verdict from it - nulling it would have made /poslanec silently stop disclosing bad dates. Commit e7bea5c.

The OG image is named in that sentence and grep for `fresh` returned zero hits. Social platforms cache that card and newsrooms screenshot it. Now permalinkCardModel (pure, tested) decides what the card may say; a stale view never gets the confirming cobalt; invalid/gone/unavailable stopped sharing one frame (our outage no longer reads as the death of a documented view); permalinkSources() is ONE rule read by both the card and isBasedOn, preferring a node's own registry links over the four blanket sources; and the evidence bundle now carries the search bound the page prints under 'bez nej by generovana cesta byla obvineni' plus absolute url/identifier from request headers. Found only by rendering the card: the font subset was requested over un-uppercased text while the card sets textTransform:uppercase, so titles drew one Archivo capital and fell to the fallback face mid-word. Commit 6f844c9.

title: The vault instructed a command that erases the effort layer from all 207 MPs; the graph writers can no longer delete each other's work
body: kg-compute rebuilt node props from scratch against an upsert that wholesale-replaces them, and frontier.md F5 (status open) prescribed --commit --reset, which also calls clearKg (~154k nodes out, ~1k back). Added a pure read-merge, a reset guard computed from what the store holds vs what the run emits, and a node-side guard in kg-promote derived deny-by-default. Six sibling scripts stopped crashing on the live graph via one shared nextPass. Commits eab0354, 7732a86, 0d89056, 4f62ca4.

title: /graf memoised a null index for the process lifetime, so an outage rendered as a real empty graph
body: graphLoader had zero reportLoaderFailure calls across nine degradation sites (the ADR said four) while eslint excluded features/graph from the rule written to catch exactly that, and lib/testing/loaders.test.ts pinned the gap as the contract. memoNonNull memoises success only; the exclusion is deleted with no suppressions; a genuinely missing node still leaves no trace, deliberately. import server-only added and proven safe by a production build. Commits 69124ae, 5707bd4, c5c838b.

title: Citations built by lib/kg/sourceLinks pointed at search pages, the wrong registry, and internal node ids
body: ~153k contract nodes cited a supplier-wide query while carrying their own canonical registry URL in props.sourceUrl; two tier:detail URLs were search endpoints; a hlidacstatu address was labelled 'Registr smluv'; citableId printed the internal bill node-id suffix as a public print number. A refuted premise died too: ingest DOES carry the notice URL (20/20 nodes). TERM_NUMBER=10 recorded as a dated limit - after the next term's ingest those citations resolve to a live page about a different bill. Commit a8ad5d1, plus c453605 for the sample graph's 404 address.
